messages.author: c21e804e07c5e732
messages.subject: pointrange with a horizontal bar?
parts:
Hi,

I wondering if there is a way to add pointrange with a horizontal bar.
Semantically this is similar to crossbar, where the width of the
crossbar indicates something. But I'd link a pointrange with a
horizontal bar for certain plots.

I don't find some a function in ggplot2. Does anybody know how to make one?

--
Regards,
Peng

messages.author: d588a03e58ea7e7f
messages.subject: Re: pointrange with a horizontal bar?
parts:
On 9/25/2011 8:06 AM, Peng Yu wrote:
> Hi,
>
> I wondering if there is a way to add pointrange with a horizontal bar.
> Semantically this is similar to crossbar, where the width of the
> crossbar indicates something. But I'd link a pointrange with a
> horizontal bar for certain plots.
>
> I don't find some a function in ggplot2. Does anybody know how to make one?

There is geom_hpointrange in the ggExtra package on R-forge
(https://r-forge.r-project.org/R/?group_id=375) which does what you
want. That will work with the current version of ggplot2, but not when
version 0.9.0 is released.


--
Brian S. Diggs, PhD
Senior Research Associate, Department of Surgery
Oregon Health & Science University

That reminds me, it sure would be nice if there were a coordinate
transform that did what coord_flip() does plus it reversed the order of
levels of a discrete x-coordinate. In other words, in your example, it
would look exactly the same except that the "Variable" axis would have A
on top and increase alphabetically downward, instead of having J on top
and decreasing alphabetically downward.

I find myself having to simulate this a lot, by forcing the "x"-axis
factor to be ordered with the levels in reverse from the way I want them.
